**Running flutter with timeout**

I’m thinking about running `flutter run` in the foreground, but I have to consider the tool’s timeout. Maybe I can use bash to implement `timeout 300`. First, I need to confirm that the VM service will appear. I’ll run the command and wait up to 240 seconds. Once the service is found, I’ll kill the process quickly and proceed with the actual screenshot attempt. Let’s get started!

arguments.command:
set -euo pipefail
LOG=/tmp/nothingness_seek_flutter.log
rm -f "$LOG"
flutter run -t dev/main_debug.dart -d linux --debug >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
BASE=""
for i in $(seq 1 240); do
  if grep -q "A Dart VM Service" "$LOG"; then
    BASE=$(grep -oE "http://127\.0\.0\.1:[0-9]+/[^ ]+" "$LOG" | tail -1 || true)
    if [[ -n "$BASE" ]]; then break; fi
  fi
  sleep 1
done
if [[ -z "$BASE" ]]; then
  echo "Failed to find VM service URL after waiting.";
  tail -n 60 "$LOG" || true
  kill $PID || true
  exit 1
fi
echo "VM_BASE=$BASE"
kill $PID || true
